survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TALIS 2013 teacher and principal questionnaire data for Korea, merging teacher and principal files after removing irrelevant variables (including weighting-related identifiers such as TCHWGT/TRWGT1/SCHWGT/SRWGT1) and standardized scores/administration identifiers. The analytic sample is restricted to middle school teachers and principals, and variables with ≥50% missingness are deleted before further processing. Missing questionnaire responses are imputed using a k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) approach (k=41 with Gower distance) after data cleaning and merging. The manuscript does not report applying TALIS complex survey weights (e.g., teacher/principal weights) in the modeling stage; given the use of penalized regression with variable selection and the absence of explicit weight application, weighting is treated as not applied/unclear for inference.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variable is the mean of 10 TALIS teacher job satisfaction Likert-type items (TT2G46A–TT2G46J), not a cognitive achievement scale generated via PVs. Missing data handling is explicitly described: after deleting variables with ≥50% missingness, the authors impute remaining missing values using k-NN with Gower distance (k=41). Therefore, there is no PV or PV-combining step to report for this outcome.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used TALIS 2013 Korea teacher and principal data. Starting from 526 teacher variables and 393 principal variables, irrelevant variables were removed (including IDs, weighting variables, standardized scores, and administration variables such as IDTEACH/IDCNTRY/TCHWGT/TRWGT1/SCHWGT/SRWGT1/IDLANG). Variables with ≥50% missingness were deleted. Categorical questionnaire items were dummy-coded, and dummy variables from the same multi-category item were treated as a group for group Mnet. After data cleaning and merging teacher and principal datasets, the final dataset contained 2,577 middle school teachers and 165 principals with 558 variables; the response variable was the mean of 10 job satisfaction items (TT2G46A–TT2G46J).

main_findings.dataset_used: TALIS 2013 (Korea) middle school teachers (teacher questionnaire) — job satisfaction
main_findings.target_variable: Teacher job satisfaction (mean of 10 Likert items)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Group Mnet (100 iterations): RMSE mean=0.393 (SD=0.008), range 0.368–0.409. Group MCP: RMSE mean=0.392 (SD=0.009). Group LASSO: RMSE mean=0.389 (SD=0.009). Variable selection: Group Mnet selected ~31.76 variables on average (SD=9.67; min=16, max=59).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TALIS 2013 (Korea) middle school teacher questionnaire the study leveraged teacher feedback, classroom climate, and participatory/caring school climate items to predict teacher job satisfaction, finding that the best-performing penalized model (Group Mnet) achieved RMSE ≈0.393 with stable selection of 18 teacher variables (selected ≥50% of runs). This indicates that improving feedback/appraisal usefulness, fostering caring and collaborative classroom/school climates, and supporting teachers’ professional learning conditions may be practical levers for raising teacher job satisfaction, though the study is predictive and does not establish causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes TALIS 2013 Korea data for 2,577 middle school teachers (and 165 principals merged into the candidate predictor set) to predict teacher job satisfaction measured as the mean of 10 Likert-type items (TT2G46A–TT2G46J). After removing variables with ≥50% missingness and dummy-coding categorical items, the authors impute remaining missing values using k-NN (k=41, Gower distance). For modeling and variable selection, they compare penalized group methods—Group Mnet (primary), Group MCP, and Group LASSO—using repeated random 7:3 train/test splits with 10-fold cross-validation on the training set and 100 repetitions. Group Mnet yields RMSE mean 0.393 (SD=0.008), with similar RMSE ranges across methods (≈0.368–0.409). The most consistently selected predictors are teacher feedback/appraisal perceptions, classroom climate items, and participatory/caring school climate items. Limitations include unclear use of TALIS sampling weights and the fact that predictive selection does not imply causality.
